title: Spark's buyback schedule is convex, returning a quarter of excess funds up to 2x target and all of it above
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.4.2.3.2 runs monthly, immediately after Spark's settlement with Sky: excess over the Target SubDAO Proxy Value "is multiplied by the Standard Buyback Rate parameter up to the Enhanced Buyback Threshold, and then by the Enhanced Buyback Rate for any amount in excess." The live parameters (.3.3) are Standard 25%, Enhanced 100%, Threshold 200% — and .3.1.4 clarifies that the threshold is expressed as a multiple of target, so "a 200% Enhanced Buyback Threshold means that the Enhanced Buyback Rate will apply to any subDAO proxy value over 2x the Target."

The three parameters resolve a genuine conflict. Returning all excess immediately maximizes value to SPK holders but leaves the treasury permanently at its floor, so any adverse month forces a raise. Returning nothing lets a treasury accumulate without limit, which is a governance risk of its own — idle capital invites reallocation fights and gives no signal that the business is generating surplus.

The kink splits the difference by *purpose*. Between 1x and 2x target, 75% of excess is retained: this is buffer-building, and the buffer is genuinely useful because the target itself ratchets on high-water marks. Above 2x, retention stops entirely — a treasury twice its own conservatively-computed requirement has no further defensive story, so 100% goes to buybacks.

Execution remains a trusted round trip rather than an automated one. A Spark proxy Spell transfers USDS to a Buyback Executor — "initially... the Spark Operations Multisig" (.3.1.5) — which purchases SPK on the open market and returns it. The policy is mechanical; the leg where the money is actually in someone's hands is not.
description: A 25% Standard Buyback Rate applies below the 200% Enhanced Buyback Threshold and a 100% Enhanced Rate above, so the treasury can build a buffer but cannot accumulate indefinitely.
